Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call changed in the uncommitted diff against 7fef5b5 and is graded against the current text. The sentences that decide it: "When a call's result is passed on, matched against or nested in another call, each of its arguments is a name or a short literal: a map, struct or keyword list that would span several lines is built first under a name that says what it is, one field per line, with a blank line between multi-line statements." and "A call whose result is itself bound to a name may take its options inline, as `formatter` does below". Ecto queries are treated as the previous grades did: a multi-line from/2 named before its Repo call is clean (it is now also a call whose result is bound to a name, so its keyword clauses may sit inline), and a multi-line query passed straight into a Repo call would be violated (the c-baseline sonnet-1 reading); no run here does the latter. A map the formatter keeps on one line is outside the rule.

Every multi-line map, struct or keyword literal inside a call, quoted, with whether the call's result is bound or passed on and whether the literal was named first. haiku-1: lines 67-71 query = / from p in Post, / where: p.user_id == ^user_id, / order_by: [desc: p.inserted_at], / preload: [:user], the from/2 keyword clauses inline in a call whose result is bound to query (allowed), then blank line 72 and line 73: Repo.all(query), whose result is returned; no other multi-line literal: its audit map is one line and named anyway (line 102: attrs = %{action: action, resource: "post", resource_id: post.id}), passed by name at line 105: |> Log.changeset(attrs), whose result is piped on to Repo.insert(). haiku-2: lines 66-71 query = / from(p in Post, / where: ..., / order_by: ..., / preload: :user / ), bound to query, blank, line 73: Repo.all(query); lines 99-104 attrs = %{ / action: "post.published", / resource: "post", / resource_id: post.id, / user_id: actor.id / }, named first, one field per line, blank line 105, then line 107: |> Log.changeset(attrs), whose result is passed on to Repo.insert(); lines 131-135 query = / from(p in Post, / where: is_nil(p.published_at), / update: [set: [published_at: p.inserted_at]] / ), bound, blank, line 137: {count, _} = Repo.update_all(query, []), matched against, takes the name. sonnet-1: lines 69-73 query = / from p in Post, ... / preload: :user, bound, blank, line 75: Repo.all(query); lines 109-112 attrs = %{ / action: "post.published", / description: "Published post #{post.id} (#{post.title})" / }, named first, blank line 113, line 115: |> Log.changeset(attrs), passed on to Repo.insert(); lines 150-153 query = / from p in "posts", / where: ..., / update: [...], bound, blank, line 155: {count, nil} = Repo.update_all(query, []), matched, takes the name. sonnet-2: lines 25-29 backfill = / from(post in "posts", ... / ), bound, blank, line 31: {count, nil} = Repo.update_all(backfill, []), matched, takes the name; lines 109-113 query = / from post in Post, ..., bound, blank, line 115: Repo.all(query); lines 154-158 attrs = %{ / action: "post.published", / user_id: post.user_id, / metadata: %{post_id: post.id, title: post.title} / }, named first, blank line 159, line 161: |> Log.changeset(attrs), passed on to Repo.insert(). No multi-line literal sits inside a call whose result is passed on, matched or nested; every controller calls render(conn, :show, post: post) on one line. The six ecto-phoenix.md rules: 1 of 4 violated, haiku-1's Keep migrations to schema changes (line 123: execute "UPDATE posts SET published_at = inserted_at" inside up/0, after the alter at 119-121; its own comment at lines 114-117 says the skill points to a separate script and that it followed the request instead), the shape graded violated in the 0397dec and db91c23 skill runs. other_violations follow the sweep-c standard: a missing @moduledoc on the context or a public context function without @doc counts under the comments rule; missing docs on schema modules, controllers and migrations do not (haiku-1's Post has no @moduledoc and its changeset/2 and publish_changeset/2 no @doc). One found: haiku-2 line 76: def get_post!(id), do: Repo.get!(Post, id) has no @doc. No single-step pipe, no pipeline starting with a call, every with has two steps. The assumption comments (haiku-1 3-9 and 27-28, haiku-2 1-4, sonnet-1 108, sonnet-2 152) and the pointers to the backfill (haiku-2 124-125, sonnet-1 132-134, sonnet-2 17-19) say what the code cannot show; haiku-1's line 139 comment on the 404 does the same.
